tools.name: get_trend
tools.title: Get a typeface's trend
tools.description: Usage rank, trending rank, 7- and 28-day rank changes, band and daily history for one Google Fonts family. Each trait or signal keeps its stable key and adds a plain-English label, a dimension (FONT, COLOR, LAYOUT or VIBE), basis (measured or ai), tier (headline, supporting or archive), momentum_index (0–100 percentile of the stored next-wave score among headline + supporting signals), confidence (High, Medium or Low, with confidence_reason) and, where staged, stage_label (Emerging, Rising, Peaking, Fading or Steady).

tools.name: audit_sites
tools.title: Competitive audit
tools.description: Compare 2–6 sites side by side: at a glance, type (faces, sizes, shared faces), color (palettes with readable names, overlap), layout and components (sites × components matrix, CSS features, stack), vibe and voice (AI-tagged estimates), versus the market (rising/emerging traits each site already shows and fading ones it still uses, read in its own sector), recent moves (90 days) and white space (traits rising in the set's main sector that none of them use). Untracked domains are listed as pending. Each trait keeps its stable key and adds label, dimension and explainer_url; audit_url opens the printable page.

domains.description: Domains such as linear.app; protocol and www. are ignored.

sector.description: Read open territory in this sector instead of the set's most common one.

tools.name: watchlist_changes
tools.title: Watchlist changes
tools.description: The same items as a watchlist's RSS feed: the last 30 days of confirmed site changes, rebrands, stage changes and alerts for its sites and signals (newest first, at most 50), plus weekly summaries. Needs the feed token from the feed URL (/api/public/watch-feed/<feed_token>.xml); rotated or unknown tokens return an error. Traits keep their stable key and add label, dimension and explainer_url.

feed_token.description: The token in the watchlist's feed URL.

tools.name: forecast_ledger
tools.title: Forecast ledger
tools.description: The durable, immutable record of slug's forecast calls and how they resolved (hit, miss, void or still open), plus the live hit rate with n. Filter by trait, scope, outcome or since. The backtest (history replay) is returned separately and is never part of the live hit rate. Each call keeps its stable trait key and adds label, dimension and explainer_url.

scope.description: all or a sector, e.g. fintech.

since.description: Only calls made on or after this date (UTC).

tools.name: stories
tools.title: Stories
tools.description: Published slug stories, newest first: what the product judged newsworthy from its own data (brand moves, rebrands, stage shifts, breakouts, first sightings, crossovers, counter-moves, white space, roundups, news naming a tracked brand). Each story has a type, headline, deck, facts with receipts (basis measured or ai), an optional why-it-matters line (basis ai, validated against the facts) or the deterministic so-what (basis measured), the newsworthiness score with its four components, and urls. Signals in signal_keys keep their stable key and add a plain-English label.

since.description: ISO date; only stories that happened on or after it.

tools.name: morning_line
tools.title: The Morning Line
tools.description: The daily edition for one UTC day (today by default): the lead story, up to five more ranked by score with their one-line why, Moving now under the run-gap rule, the opening (best white-space story of the week not used in the last three editions), the figure and what the desk held. Finished days never change.

date.description: UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

tools.name: sector_report
tools.title: State of a sector
tools.description: The quarterly report for one sector, built from stored data: headline signals with stage and share against all sectors (Momentum is all-sector only and reported once as momentum_all_sectors), what is rising only here (and the reverse), white space, counter-moves, leading brands with their latest move, pattern examples and the quarter's stories. No AI text.

tools.name: data_stories
tools.title: Data stories
tools.description: slug data stories: one question about how brands look on the web, answered step by step from stored captures. Without slug: the numbered list with status. With slug: the question, every step as text with its figures and receipts, and what the numbers are based on.

slug.description: A data story slug from the list, e.g. who-went-big-first.
